title: Primary Care Provider Assignment Practice Types: Member Eligibility Schedule
content:
Which of the seven practice types of the **Primary Care Provider Assignment** a member may be assigned to depends on the member's age, recorded sex and, for two practice types, an active care enrollment.

## Rule

- A member may be assigned only to a practice type whose age range contains the member's age in completed years on the assignment's effective date, and to an **OB/GYN Primary Care Provider** only when the member is recorded as female.
- Holding a care enrollment changes which practice types are open to the member: **Specialist Serving as PCP** and **Health Home Lead Provider** are available only to a member who holds an active care enrollment in one of the tiers listed for that practice type.
- For a practice type with a care enrollment prerequisite, the member's care enrollment (Care Management) in a listed tier must be in **active** status on the request date. This is read from the system record of that care enrollment before the assignment is made.
- A member who reaches the practice type's maximum age is told the practice type's age-out notice days before the birthday and, without a choice, is reassigned by the plan effective the first day of the month after the birthday.

## Schedule

| Practice type | Providers of this type | Youngest age | Oldest age | Female members only | Care enrollment required (active, one of) | Age-out notice days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Primary Care Provider | Family medicine, internal medicine or general practice | 0 | 120 | No | None | 0 |
| Pediatric Primary Care Provider | Pediatrics | 0 | 20 | No | None | 60 |
| OB/GYN Primary Care Provider | Obstetrics and gynecology | 12 | 120 | Yes | None | 0 |
| Federally Qualified Health Center Home | A federally qualified health center or rural health clinic | 0 | 120 | No | None | 0 |
| Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice | A practice with NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home recognition | 0 | 120 | No | None | 0 |
| Specialist Serving as PCP | A specialist serving a member with a qualifying chronic condition | 18 | 120 | No | Complex Case Management or Health Home Services | 0 |
| Health Home Lead Provider | A provider with state health home designation | 0 | 120 | No | Health Home Services | 0 |

An oldest age of 120 means the practice type has no upper age limit, and an age-out notice of 0 days means the practice type has no age limit to give notice of.

## Cases (hypothetical members)

- A female member aged 11 in completed years on the effective date is outside the OB/GYN Primary Care Provider range (12 to 120); at 12 she is inside it.
- A male member aged 30 cannot be assigned to an OB/GYN Primary Care Provider, whatever his age.
- A member aged 40 whose Complex Case Management enrollment is active on the request date may be assigned to a Specialist Serving as PCP; if that enrollment is not in active status on the request date, that practice type is not open to the member.
- A member with an active Health Home Services enrollment meets the care enrollment requirement of both the Specialist Serving as PCP and the Health Home Lead Provider practice types.
- A member with a Pediatric Primary Care Provider whose birthday of reaching the maximum age falls on 14 August is told 60 days before, on 15 June; without a choice, the plan reassignment takes effect on 1 September.
